Virtual assistant for consulting firms

Keep appointments, onboarding records and deliverables organised for advisers and client service teams.

A client intake virtual assistant can schedule first meetings, request the agreed documents and show which records are missing. The engagement owner sees what’s ready for review and who should handle the next question.

For existing accounts, we track client feedback, follow up on sign-offs and turn meeting notes into an action list. The project lead approves commitments and deliverables.

Prepare a consultation without exposing client material

Your client intake virtual assistant can prepare the consultation details. A virtual assistant for consultants should keep sensitive materials in the approved client workspace.

A prospective client asks for an introductory appointment and sends a document that belongs in the firm’s approved intake channel. The client intake virtual assistant’s role is to route the request, prepare a useful appointment brief and leave the acceptance decision with the appropriate professional.

  1. 01

    Create the initial enquiry record

    Record the source and category of the request using the fields the firm approves. Give the enquiry an owner and use the approved route to ask for missing details. Keep sensitive content out of the general scheduling record.

  2. 02

    Prepare a review-ready appointment

    Confirm the time and the people who should attend. Use the intake checklist to show which items are complete and what still needs review. Link to approved source material rather than attaching extra copies to the invite.

  3. 03

    Record the decision and follow-up

    After the appointment, assign the agreed next action and due date. Route questions about acceptance, terms or fees to the engagement owner. Keep any draft proposal separate until the named professional approves it.

Prepare the inputs and rules.

A virtual assistant for consulting firms needs one routine enquiry and one exception. Your client intake virtual assistant can use both to check the intake rules.

Intake checklist

Agree the minimum information required to route an enquiry and identify what can only be collected through a private channel. Test the checklist with a typical request and an incomplete one.

File handling

Specify the approved workspace, naming rules and who can access each folder. Agree whether a client intake virtual assistant can move, copy or remove files and how changes should be recorded.

Client commitments

Identify who approves fees, deliverables and deadlines. Provide wording for administrative acknowledgements and a separate route for requests that need professional judgment.

Decide what happens when the normal rule fails.

Your client intake virtual assistant should flag a request needing professional judgment. Your virtual assistant for consultants can collect the question for the responsible professional.

An enquiry arrives with confidential information

Use the firm’s approved route for the material and notify the owner. Keep only the minimum reference needed to track the request.

A proposed deadline is outside ordinary capacity

Check existing work and bring the decision to the engagement owner. Record the date requested and the next step without promising an outcome.

A draft changes the scope or fee

Show the changed terms and route the draft to the authorised person. Keep it in review until the firm confirms the version that can be shared.

Check the work against the original brief.

Review your virtual assistant for consulting firms against promised follow-ups. Your client intake virtual assistant should distinguish missing client information from an internal review delay.

Intake completeness

Sample recent appointment briefs and check whether each shows an owner, missing information and the next action. Identify what required a second request.

Document trace

Confirm that client files were recorded in the correct location and access matched the approved list. Check that general calendar entries do not carry confidential details.

Follow-up consistency

Review open proposals and onboarding tasks for a date, accountable owner and last approved version. Move unresolved decisions back to the relevant professional.

Leave a record the next person can use.

A virtual assistant for consultants should leave the next action and deadline together. Your virtual assistant for consulting firms also needs the latest client communication.

Part of the handoverWhat to recordWhat the next owner can do
Current workWhat to recordInclude the latest version, the source link and the current status. Note what was already checked and which changes were approved.What the next owner can doContinue from the latest approved state without searching for the source or repeating a completed check.
Open decisionsWhat to recordList each outstanding decision, the person who can make it and the point at which the next owner should follow up.What the next owner can doPrioritise the blocked items and ask a specific question when the next approval is due.
Time-sensitive commitmentsWhat to recordState the time zone, the next update due and any commitments that someone has already shared. Include the agreed backup contact.What the next owner can doKeep the next promise visible and make sure requests that cannot wait reach the correct person.
Changes to the instructionsWhat to recordRecord which rule changed, who approved it and when it starts. Keep an example that shows the difference in practice.What the next owner can doUse the current rule and compare new work with the agreed example during the next review.

Plan a virtual assistant for consultants

Plan your client intake virtual assistant around consultation windows. A virtual assistant for consultants needs a backup contact when the main reviewer is unavailable.

First enquiry

Capture contact details, the broad request and availability using approved intake fields. Flag requests needing a conflict or eligibility check for the responsible professional before confirming scope or making a commitment.

Before the consultation

Confirm the slot and meeting format. Record which materials were requested and where the client should submit them. Keep detailed records within the approved client workspace.

After the consultation

Log the next action, the responsible person and any deadline promised to the client. Record whether the team is waiting for internal review, additional information or a decision to begin work so another person can follow up.

Frequently Asked Questions

Ask which information a virtual assistant for consulting firms should collect. Your client intake virtual assistant should route eligibility, advice and engagement decisions to your team.

Can you help collect client documents?

Yes, within the agreed intake checklist and approved storage channels. Your team decides what sensitive documents are required and who can access them.

Who signs off on proposals or invoices?

The client intake virtual assistant can prepare drafts and track status. An authorised person at the firm approves terms, fees and issuance.

Can you coordinate consultation appointments?

A virtual assistant for consultants can collect availability, prepare meeting details and maintain the schedule within agreed rules. Give the client intake virtual assistant the approved appointment windows and the person who can authorise an exception or a new commitment.

What happens when an enquiry requires professional advice?

A client intake virtual assistant can record the question and organise the approved background information. The responsible professional reviews the request and provides any advice, eligibility decision or commitment about the services the firm will deliver.

How are client follow-ups managed?

Your virtual assistant for consulting firms can record the next action, deadline and responsible person after an enquiry or meeting. Agree how to distinguish a request waiting on client information from one needing an internal decision.

What do we need to provide before starting?

Bring an intake example, approved information fields, consultation rules and a named reviewer. Confirm where client material belongs and who can access it so the first task follows the firm’s working practices.
